mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Monday 4:06 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-23 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
items.about: Sells servers, storage, networking and hybrid-cloud services to businesses.
items.why: HPE jumped about 18% as Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang lifted AI-hardware names across the board. Posts link reports that server makers are pushing higher prices on already-signed AI server deals to offset memory costs, ahead of HPE's fiscal Q4 report, expected in early December (date not yet confirmed).

items.name: GameStop
items.about: Video-game and collectibles retailer that also holds bitcoin on its balance sheet.
items.why: GameStop rose about 2.5% to close near $27.33, and its large retail following pushed it up the board. Posts say the stock has broken above a multi-year chart level; no company news was cited in the stream.

items.name: CrowdStrike
items.about: Cybersecurity company best known for its Falcon endpoint-protection platform.
items.why: CrowdStrike fell about 9% after agreeing to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing it at about $43.9 billion (1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share), per its SEC filing. The company says the deal moves it into network security and should lift free cash flow per share at close; buyers typically fall on large stock-funded deals as the market weighs dilution.

items.name: Zscaler
items.about: Cloud security company whose Zero Trust platform secures users' connections to apps and the internet.
items.why: Zscaler jumped about 18% after CrowdStrike agreed to acquire it for 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share, valuing it at about $43.9 billion. Posts say it also beat Q1 revenue and EPS estimates and withdrew guidance because of the deal; the stock closed below the implied deal value as CRWD fell.

items.name: NVIDIA
items.about: Designs the GPUs and networking gear that power most AI data centers.
items.why: Nvidia soared about 31%, adding a record amount of market value, after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO 12 days after accepting his resignation. The stock had dropped about 23% in the week after he left; reports say an investigation tied to his departure continues and posts say US officials pushed for his return.

items.name: SpaceX
items.about: Rocket launch and Starlink satellite-internet company.
items.why: SpaceX rose about 4% but closed roughly $8 below its intraday high, lagging AI names that gained 20–40%. Posts focus on the fade and on talk of a merger; no company news was cited.

items.name: Applied Digital
items.about: Builds and operates data centers for AI and high-performance computing customers.
items.why: Applied Digital jumped about 20% as Nvidia's CEO reversal sparked a rebound across AI data-center stocks after last week's selloff. Posts say company press releases were overshadowed by the Nvidia news.

items.name: Occidental Petroleum
items.about: US oil and gas producer with chemical and carbon-capture businesses.
items.why: Occidental slipped about 2% as Brent crude fell about 3.7% to roughly $86.6 and money rotated back into tech. Posts also discuss Middle East headlines that have kept oil volatile.

items.name: Anthropic
items.about: AI company behind the Claude models, listed on Nasdaq since Nov 19.
items.why: Anthropic, which priced its record IPO at $83 last week and opened at $111.50, swung between about $85 and $94 before closing down about 1.4%. Chatter stayed extremely high as traders debated the post-IPO fade while other AI names rallied.

items.name: Intellia Therapeutics
items.about: Develops CRISPR-based gene-editing treatments.
items.why: Intellia swung between $9.70 and $10.68 before closing up about 1.5%. Posts cite a March 10, 2027 FDA decision date for lonvo-z and debate whether its cash, which management says lasts into 2028, will need topping up before a launch.

items.name: SELLAS Life Sciences
items.about: Biotech developing the cancer vaccine galinpepimut-S for leukemia.
items.why: SELLAS eased about 3% as it consolidates after the Nov 17 Phase 3 REGAL readout, in which its vaccine cut the risk of death by 41% (median survival 24.0 vs 14.7 months). The company plans an FDA filing in the first half of 2027; posts say a buyout could follow, which is unconfirmed.

items.name: Dell Technologies
items.about: Sells PCs, servers and storage, including AI server systems.
items.why: Dell surged about 21% with the AI-hardware rebound after Nvidia reinstated Huang. Posts cite reports of higher prices on signed AI server orders and note Dell reports fiscal Q3 results on Tuesday, Nov 24, against a prior outlook of about $49B revenue.

items.name: Eli Lilly
items.about: Drugmaker behind the obesity and diabetes treatments Zepbound and Mounjaro.
items.why: Lilly rose about 1.5%, holding up on a day when money rotated back into tech. Posts tie it to SELLAS buyout speculation and drug-pricing debate, neither backed by company news.

items.name: Symbotic
items.about: Builds AI-driven robotic warehouse automation systems, with Walmart as its largest customer.
items.why: Symbotic rose about 12% in regular trading, then fell after hours following its fiscal Q4 report: revenue of $778M (+26%) near the top of guidance and adjusted EBITDA of $114M above it. It also cited an expanded Walmart agreement and expects faster revenue growth next quarter.

items.name: Global X Dow 30 Covered Call ETF
items.about: Holds the 30 Dow stocks and sells call options on the index for income.
items.why: The fund rose about 2.3% as the Dow gained about 3% in the best day for US stocks since April 2025. Its ticker draws broad market chatter from traders discussing whether last week's selloff has bottomed.

items.name: Broadcom
items.about: Makes custom AI accelerators, networking chips and infrastructure software.
items.why: Broadcom gained about 3%, far less than most chip stocks on the Nvidia-led rebound, and posts complain about the lag. Posts also cite TSMC executives saying AI chip demand remains strong with no order changes.

items.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (ADR)
items.about: World's largest contract chipmaker, producing chips for Nvidia, Apple and others.
items.why: TSMC's ADR jumped about 14% as Nvidia's reinstatement of Huang revived the AI-chip trade. Posts relay TSMC executives saying no customers have changed orders and that leading-edge demand remains very strong.

items.name: Meta Platforms
items.about: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp and spends heavily on AI.
items.why: Meta rose about 6.6% in the broad tech rebound after falling about 12.6% last week, per posts. Posts debate whether heavy AI data-center spending is crowding out buybacks.

items.name: Apple
items.about: Makes the iPhone, Mac and related services.
items.why: Apple added about 2% on the market-wide rebound, trailing chip and AI names. Posts discuss its valuation versus other mega-caps; no company-specific news was cited.

items.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Natural Gas
items.about: Leveraged ETF that aims for twice the daily move of natural gas futures.
items.why: BOIL fell about 13%, meaning natural gas futures dropped roughly 6–7% on the day given its 2x leverage. Posts cite Permian pipelines coming into service; the specific cause wasn't confirmed in news searches.
